scope: Numerical diagnosis; not a new physical performance benchmark
finding: Ancilla.amplitude uses a piecewise-constant position wavefunction. Its jumps can generate artificial high-momentum tails; the underlying step-function approximation has no finite continuum kinetic energy.
mathematical_diagnostic: For derivative half-step h<dx/2, integral |dphi/dx|^2 for the step function behaves as sum(jump^2)/(2h), diverging as h approaches zero.
interpretation: Average heating is consistent with finite-energy SUM backaction, but the abrupt rare spikes cannot be labeled physical until smooth measurement-resource evaluation is checked.
required_followup: Replace binwise amplitude evaluation with a smooth analytic resource and consistent continuous outcome sampling. Validate against explicit two-mode QuTiP and rerun numerical checks before long-horizon physical claims.
existing_two_cycle_results: Passed limited bin/cutoff fidelity refinements for seven of nine cases. This does not validate long-time energy tails.
cutoff5120_check: Still useful for basis sensitivity; does not by itself resolve the measurement-approximation concern.
